title: Bail under NDPS - the toughest bail provision in Indian law
p1:
Getting bail in a normal criminal case can already be difficult. But what happens when the case falls under the NDPS Act?

Many people assume bail is a basic right once a person spends time in custody. Under NDPS law, the reality can be very different.
p2:
A lesser-known fact: for serious drug offences involving commercial quantities, the court does not simply ask whether the accused will appear for trial. The law creates a much stricter test before granting bail.

The accused has to show that there are reasonable grounds to believe they may not be guilty and that they are unlikely to commit another offence while on bail.
p3:
This is why NDPS bail is considered one of the toughest bail provisions in India. Even before the trial begins, the court must carefully examine the case materials and legal requirements.

The practical lesson: in NDPS matters, small details like the quantity involved, recovery procedure, and evidence collection can significantly affect bail chances.
conclusion: Do you think strict NDPS bail provisions are necessary to control drug offences, or do they create challenges for genuine accused persons?
